lvc541a_current_ratings.document: TI SN54LVC541A, SN74LVC541A Octal Buffers/Drivers, SCAS298N (January 1993, revised June 2014), served by LCSC for C113281
lvc541a_current_ratings.shows: Absolute Maximum Ratings: continuous output current +-50 mA, and continuous current through VCC or GND +-100 mA. The second is the package total; the first is per output. The review note recorded '50 mA per part', which is neither - it is the per-output figure read as a package one, and it was the floor used for the gate-line pull-down resistance.

lvc541a_dc_limits.assumes: that 4 pF is usable as a maximum. The row has a single column under TYP and no MAX at all, so it is a typical being read as though it were a bound - the same species as the LAN8742A's supply current, and covered by the same instruction to measure it on the first assembled board
lvc541a_dc_limits.document: TI SN54LVC541A, SN74LVC541A, SCAS298N (January 1993, revised June 2014), served by LCSC for C113281
lvc541a_dc_limits.shows: Input capacitance C_i = 4 pF at V_CC = 3.3 V, which is what the trip-chain deck needs: the latch's one Q output holds both buffers' second enable as well as the gate-kill transistor's gate, and the design check gives each of them the full 24 mA by taking a max over them rather than letting them share it. Also V_OL = 0.55 V at I_OL = 24 mA, the figure behind this part's 24 mA rating.
